ProjulCreateMessageConfig.description: Add a message to a record.

idempotency_key.description: Reuse the same key and body for safe replay (24 hours).
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

parent_id.description: The parent's opaque id, carrying that record type's own prefix.
parent_id.title: Parent Id

message_type.description: Free text. Projul defines no vocabulary for it.
message_type.title: Message Type

contact_method.description: One of `phone`, `email`, `text`, `person`, or `null` to leave it unset. Matching is case-insensitive, and the labels the Projul UI shows for the same four (`Phone Call`, `Text Message`, `In Person`) are accepted and stored as the value above. Anything else is `422 validation_failed` with `invalid_enum`: Projul renders a communication record by matching these values exactly, so storing another spelling would file a record the app cannot display.
contact_method.title: Contact Method

contact_direction.description: One of `in`, `out`, or `null`. `Inbound`/`Received` and `Outbound`/`Sent` are accepted as aliases, case-insensitively, and stored as `in`/`out`. Anything else is `422 validation_failed`. Leave it `null` for an in-person contact and report the outcome with `contact_success`.
contact_direction.title: Contact Direction

name.description: Restrict to the clients whose name matches this value. The match is the client's first and last name joined with a single space (for example `Dana Whitfield`), compared case-insensitively and ignoring leading and trailing spaces. It is a whole-name match, not a substring search, and does not consider the company name. A value that matches nothing returns an empty page, never an error. A value of only spaces is `400 invalid_request`.
name.title: Name

email.description: Restrict to the clients that carry this email address on the client record or on any of its contacts. The match is case-insensitive and ignores leading and trailing spaces. A value that matches nothing returns an empty page, never an error. A value of only spaces is `400 invalid_request`.
email.title: Email

phone.description: Restrict to the clients that carry this phone number on the client record or on any of its contacts. The value you send is reduced to its digits. The stored number is compared with its spaces, dashes, parentheses, plus signs, dots and slashes removed, and an 11-digit number's leading `1` (the US and Canada country code) is dropped, so `+1 208 555 0134`, `(208) 555-0134` and `2085550134` are all the same number. A number stored with any other character in it will not match: a note in the field such as `555-0134 (cell)` or `555-0134 x12`, or an unusual dash or space pasted in from another system. Store numbers plainly. Only the number is compared; a phone's `extension` field is not considered. Numbers are not unique: a spouse or an office line can sit on several clients, so the page can hold more than one row, newest first. A value with fewer than 7 digits in it is `400 invalid_request`. A value that matches nothing returns an empty page, never an error.
phone.title: Phone

company_name.description: Restrict to the clients whose `company_name` matches this value, compared case-insensitively and ignoring leading and trailing spaces. It is a whole-value match, not a substring search, and does not consider the person's name; combine it with `name` to pin down one person at a company. A value that matches nothing returns an empty page, never an error. A value of only spaces is `400 invalid_request`.
company_name.title: Company Name

include_archived.description: `true` also lists archived clients, each carrying `status: Archived`, so a search can find a returning client and unarchive it instead of creating a duplicate. Deleted clients are never listed. An archived client still `404`s on `GET /v1/customers/{customer_id}` and cannot be linked to a new project or estimate until it is unarchived. Any value other than `true` or `false` is `400 invalid_request`.
include_archived.title: Include Archived

project_number.description: Restrict to the projects whose `project_number` matches this value. The number is compared as ONE whole value, exactly as the Projul app shows it and this API returns it, including any prefix or suffix the tenant's numbering rules add: `P-1042` matches `P-1042`, and `1042` does not. The comparison is case-insensitive and ignores leading and trailing spaces. The intended way to find the project named on a document or in an email. Projul does not guarantee the formatted number is unique, so read the page rather than assuming one row. A value that matches nothing returns an empty page, never an error. A value of only spaces is `400 invalid_request`.
project_number.title: Project Number

name.description: Restrict to the projects whose `name` matches this value, compared case-insensitively and ignoring leading and trailing spaces. It is a whole-name match, not a substring search. Project names are not unique, so read the page rather than assuming one row; combine it with `customer_id` to pin down one client's job. A value of only spaces is `400 invalid_request`. A value that matches nothing returns an empty page, never an error. It matches a project's own name only: a project with no name of its own, which reads with the name the Projul app shows for it, is found by `customer_id` instead.
name.title: Name

external_ref.title: External Ref

name.description: Restrict to the tasks whose `name` matches this value, compared case-insensitively and ignoring leading and trailing spaces. It is a whole-name match, not a substring search. Task names are not unique (each project can have its own "Site walk"), so combine it with `project_id` and read the page rather than assuming one row. A repeating task is ONE row however often it repeats, and adding `scheduled_from`/`scheduled_to` drops it unless its stored window falls in the range. A value that matches nothing returns an empty page, never an error. A value of only spaces is `400 invalid_request`.
name.title: Name

scheduled_from.description: Restrict to tasks that have a scheduled window starting at or after this instant. This filters on the schedule (the `assignments` window start), NOT on when the task row was last changed. Use it with `scheduled_to` to bound a date range; a task matches when one of its windows starts inside the range. A repeating task matches only on its stored window, never on the occurrences its rule produces, so a series that falls inside a later range is not returned. There is no `is_recurring` filter: list without the schedule filters, keep the rows whose `is_recurring` is true, and work out their dates from `recurring_rule`.
scheduled_from.title: Scheduled From

scheduled_to.description: Restrict to tasks that have a scheduled window starting at or before this instant. This filters on the schedule (the `assignments` window start), NOT on when the task row was last changed. Use it with `scheduled_from` to bound a date range. Like `scheduled_from`, it never matches the occurrences of a repeating task, only its stored window.
scheduled_to.title: Scheduled To

assignee.description: Restrict to tasks that have this person on one of their schedule windows. Pass the person's `user_` id (from a task's `assignments[].user_ids`). A value that matches nothing returns an empty page, never an error.
assignee.title: Assignee
